newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian spending abroad increases - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian spending abroad increases - newspaper.

text.p: Brazilians spent $1.5 billion abroad in the first four months of this year, 35 percent more than in the same period last year, a newspaper said.
This figure compares with the $314 million spent in Brazil by foreign tourists as calculated by the Central Bank, Jornal do Brasil said.

During the 1980s, remittances from tourists in Brazil exceeded expenditure by Brazilians abroad by an average of $407 million per year, according to Brazil's tourism agency Embratur, Jornal do Brasil said.
But with the introduction of a strong currency the picture has been reversed in the 1990s, with Brazil running an average annual deficit of $1 billion, Embratur said.
The figures are worrying the government because they contribute to Brazil's ballooning trade deficit which amounted to $3.9 billion between January and April this year, Jornal do Brasil said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
